chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he was asked:

about food in which some of it is mixed with some other, and some of it is better than some other. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If both are seen together, there is no problem, as long as the good does not cover the bad.'

key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for mixing good and bad food according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ghabn' (deception) in commercial transactions, ruling that mixing high and low-quality goods is permissible provided the superior portion remains visually distinct to prevent consumer deception. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on transparency and fairness in trade, ensuring that the buyer is not misled by the appearance of uniformity when quality varies. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for modern Islamic commercial law regarding mixed batches of goods.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim,
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>

having been asked about the foodstuff, some with the others, and some of it is fresher than some’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When you see the whole of it, so there is no problem for as long as the fresher does not cover the spoilt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, was asked
about foodstuff of high and low quality mixed together. He (the Imam) said, ‘If they see all of it, it is not harmful as long as that of good quality does not cover that of low quality.’”
